answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent network can require sequential proof-of-work puzzles for identity creation. An agent tracking a forest ember, mapping an arid knoll, or inspecting quarry marble must solve an unparallelizable time-lock puzzle. This imposes a verifiable cost in dedicated execution time per identity, preventing instant virtual cloning. However, this computational latency delays honest nodes joining the system and favors adversaries operating custom high-frequency processors.
